title: fastText AG News word bigram method check
question: With all other fastText settings held constant, does enabling word bigrams improve top-1 accuracy on the published AG News test split?
keywords: Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification

seedSources.title: Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification
seedSources.abstract: The paper presents fastText as a simple and efficient text classifier and evaluates it on text classification benchmarks. This task checks a word n-gram design choice on AG News; it does not claim to reproduce the paper's full table.

seedSources.title: Official fastText AG News classification reproduction script
seedSources.abstract: The official script downloads AG News and trains fastText with wordNgrams=2, dim=10, epoch=5, and learning rate 0.25 for this dataset.

seedSources.title: Character-level Convolutional Networks for Text Classification
seedSources.abstract: This paper introduced several large-scale text classification datasets, including the AG News benchmark used here.

experiment.protocol: Each command trains the same fastText configuration on the full published AG News split for three paired seeds 11, 23, and 47. The only treatment factor is wordNgrams=1 versus wordNgrams=2. Each command reports per-seed accuracy and the mean; no test-set tuning is allowed.
experiment.successCriterion: The word-bigram candidate supports this bounded hypothesis if its mean test accuracy across the three paired training seeds exceeds the unigram baseline mean. This is a descriptive result on one fixed AG News test split; no statistical-significance threshold is claimed.
